subject: Auto-calibration not done for hip-worn Actigraph data

messages.author: a3527f6489543e9b
messages.subject: Auto-calibration not done for hip-worn Actigraph data
parts:
Hi all

I've analysed the 24-hour hip-worn Actigraph data using GGIR, and I noticed that the auto-calibration procedure was not performed. I didn't get any errors or warning messages about the analysis, and the data files that I have are pretty good in terms of wear time compliance. 

I have attached the data quality report as well as my script below if that helps with the investigation:

GGIR(
  mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
  datadir="", 
  outputdir="", 
  do.report=c(2,4,5),do.enmo=TRUE, acc.metric="ENMO", 
  #=====================
  # Part 2
  #=====================
  strategy = 1,
  hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
  includedaycrit = 16,
  qwindow=c(0,24),
  mvpathreshold =c(143),
  bout.metric = 6,
  #=====================
  # Part 3 + 4
  #=====================
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  HASPT.algo = "HorAngle",
  sensor.location = "hip",
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  includenightcrit = 16,
  #=====================
  # Part 5
  #=====================
  threshold.lig = c(64), threshold.mod = c(143), threshold.vig = c(465),
  boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
  minimum_MM_length.part5 = 24,
  #=====================
  # Visual report
  #=====================
  timewindow = c("MM"),
  visualreport=TRUE)

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Auto-calibration not done for hip-worn Actigraph data
parts:
Hi John,

Auto-calibration is not done when there are not enough points around the sphere (see cited paper in the documentation). This is more likely when the accelerometer is not worn for a substantial part of the recording, when the recording is short (e.g. a day or less), and/or when worn on a body location that rarely is upside down (hip, chest, thigh, ankle, ...). 

If auto-calibration cannot be done consider using the calibration coefficients from a different recording with the same device or using an acceleration metric that is less sensitive to calibration error.

Cheers,
Vincent
